overview: LiquidSense's Criticals fakes the falling state vanilla requires for a critical hit, with thirteen selectable modes. Everything runs from onAttack, gated by an on-ground requirement, environment checks (ladder, web, water, lava, riding), a hurt-time filter on the target, a Fly-module guard, and an MSTimer delay (0-1000ms). The packet modes inject two to four C03PacketPlayer variants into the stream around each attack - C06 pos/look packets at offsets like 0.0425/0.0015/0.014 with onGround false, C04 position-only packets with onGround false and sub-millimetre jitter, or the packet mode's onGround-true lift of 0.0625 - so the server-side fall distance ticks above zero at hit time. The jump modes instead move the real player (motionY 0.42, 0.3425 or 0.1, or TP-hop C04 pairs of 0.02/0.01) so the attack lands mid-air, and NoGround and NGJump additionally rewrite every outgoing C03's onGround flag to false. Every mode finishes with a client-side onCriticalHit call that only plays particles.

sections.p: onAttack returns unless the target is an EntityLivingBase and the player is on ground, off ladders, webs, water, lava and mounts, the target's hurtTime is at or below the HurtTime value (default 10), Fly is off, and the MSTimer delay has passed. The packet modes then inject their offsets ahead of the attack's C02. NewPacket sends four C04 packets at 0.00521, 0.0052, 0.05 and 1.086765133E-10, each plus Random().nextDouble() / 4789 jitter, all onGround false. Packet sends C04(y + 0.0625, onGround true), C04(y, false), C04(y + 1.1E-5, false), C04(y, false). AAC4 sends 0.0525/0.0015/0.014/0.0015 all false. HypixelPacket sends 0.0425, 0.0015 and a random 0.012-or-0.014, each plus +/-1E-8..1E-7 jitter, only on even ticksExisted. NewHypixel sends four C06 pos/look packets (0.04250000001304, 0.00150000001304, 0.01400000001304, 0.00150000001304) all onGround false through the Crit() helper. All five call onCriticalHit for the particles.

The movement modes alter the real player. Hop sets motionY 0.1, fallDistance 0.1 and onGround false, so the next movement packet carries a small hop. TPHop sends C04(y + 0.02, false) then C04(y + 0.01, false) and setPosition(y + 0.01); AAC4.4.0 is the same sequence gated on motionX == 0 and motionZ == 0. Jump, HYTJump and NGJump set motionY 0.42 (the vanilla jump velocity) and suppress sprinting; LowJump sets 0.3425. NoGround calls jump() on enable and its onPacket handler rewrites every outgoing C03's onGround to false; NGJump does the same rewrite on top of its jump, and both clear sprint in onUpdate. The flag rewrites are the mode's whole point for NoGround: the client jumps once on enable and then every movement packet claims airborne, so any attack made while the module is on is server-side a mid-air hit.

Each packet mode adds three to four C03-family packets at the attack tick, all ahead of the attack's C02, with onGround false except the packet mode's first 0.0625 lift. The sub-pixel jitter (1E-8 and nextDouble()/4789) is sized to dodge movement-threshold checks that treat tiny deltas as noise, and the 0.0 entries in the offset arrays let some injected packets repeat the exact position. The C06 packets in NewHypixel additionally carry the player's current yaw and pitch, so they read as normal look-position updates. Against a server, the observable stream is a burst of three to four extra movement packets per attack, then the attack while the fall distance is nonzero.

files.label: Criticals.kt (module logic)
files.explanation: The file is the mode table plus the three handlers that execute it. The value block declares the Mode list (thirteen entries), the Delay (0-1000ms), and HurtTime; the offset arrays (hypixelOffsets, offsets, sb, motion) are the payload constants for the packet modes. onEnable performs the NoGround/NGJump jump, onUpdate clears sprint for the two sprint-sensitive modes, onPacket rewrites the onGround flag for NoGround and NGJump, and onAttack contains the gate and the when-dispatch over all thirteen modes. Crit() is the shared C06 pos/look injector used by NewHypixel. The tag getter returns the active mode, which is how the module displays its state in the client's HUD.

files.label: RandomUtils.java (jitter source)
files.explanation: RandomUtils provides the jitter the offset modes use to look organic. nextDouble(startInclusive, endInclusive) returns start plus (end - start) * Math.random(), and HypixelPacket calls it with +/-1E-8..1E-7 bounds to smear each injected offset; NewPacket uses java.util.Random's nextDouble() / 4789 directly, producing jitter up to about 2.1E-4 per packet. The magnitude is deliberate: the offsets themselves are in the 1E-5..0.05 range and the jitter is several orders below the smallest offset, so it never changes the server's fall-distance accounting, only the exact float values the server sees - the anti-pattern-detection layer. The same utility backs other modules' randomization, but here it is the only thing standing between a perfectly periodic offset burst and one with per-packet float noise.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical movement envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly rebuilds the allowed vertical movement from physics instead of trusting the packet. The vertical allowance comes from vDistRel, which seeds the allowed distance from the previous move's momentum and accepts only a few named envelopes: a zero-y move on ground, a real jump, a step-up and a riptide launch; the violation is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100 with a set-back to the stored location. Critically, fromOnGround and toOnGround come from RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround(), which ray-traces the block cache instead of reading the packet's onGround flag.\n\nEvery packet mode fails the envelope directly: the injected C04/C06 lifts (0.0015 up to 0.0625, plus the 0.05 NewPacket step) are up-moves from a standing position with no jump input, so the allowed distance stays zero and yDistanceAboveLimit is the offset itself - the 0.0625 claim travels with onGround true, but the ray trace reports ground under the player, and the flag does not relax the envelope. The packet mode's 1.1E-5 packet is under the noise floor and passes by itself, but it is always bundled with the 0.0625 lift. The 0.42 jump modes sit inside the real-jump envelope, which is why they need the jump-phase rule in fight.Critical and the SmallHop check rather than this one.

countering.label: fight.Critical (critical-hit validation)
countering.explanation: NCP's fight.Critical runs whenever the server sees a critical (mcFallDistance > 0) and applies three illegality rules. The divergence rule - Math.abs(ncpFallDistance - mcFallDistance) > 1e-5 while the player is judged on-ground - is the direct hit on the packet modes: NCP's own fall accounting (data.noFallFallDistance) says the player never left the ground, while the server-side fallDistance ticks up from the claimed 0.0015..0.0625 offsets, and NCP's ray trace still reports ground, so the difference exceeds the tolerance, criticalVL rises and the configured actions cancel the hit. The jump-phase rule - sfJumpPhase between 1 and the lift-off envelope's max phase, no collision above 0.2, and no block-bounce velocity origin - catches the jump modes: attacking within the first phases of a jump is illegal, so the Jump/HYTJump/NGJump 0.42 jumps only pass if the attack waits out the jump phases. The reset-condition rule (water, webs, climbables, etc.) kills crits claimed from blocks where the game would reset fall distance.

countering.label: Criticals (combat-side vertical check)
countering.explanation: Arc v2's Criticals check is the most direct counter: on every attack it reads Arc's physics-derived ground state (data.isOnGround(), maintained by Arc's own MovingListener from world collision, not from the packet flag) and the vertical speed of the current move; when the player is on the ground and the vertical speed is below 0.37 it raises 'critical while onGround' and flags.\n\nEvery packet-offset mode produces a vertical speed of 0.0015 to 0.0625, orders of magnitude under the 0.37 floor that a real jump (0.42) clears - the 0.0625/0.001 pair, the AAC4 0.0525/0.0015 sequence and the HypixelPacket 0.0425/0.0015 alternation all violate on the first attack. Only the 0.42 jump modes pass the vertical threshold, and those are the modes NCP's jump-phase rule is waiting for. Because the ground state is Arc's own collision result, the NoGround and NGJump onGround=false rewrites are irrelevant to it - the flag lies are ignored and the physics-derived state decides.

countering.label: SmallHop (mini-jump detection)
countering.explanation: Hawk's SmallHop exists specifically because 'small jumps can be exploited to bypass other checks such as speed and criticals'. It flags a move where wasOnGround is true, deltaY is in (0, 0.4), prevDeltaY is at or below 0, the player is not flying, not in accepted knockback and not on a slime bounce, no ladder/vine or adjacent solid is involved, and AdjacentBlocks.onGroundReally at the destination is false - then punishes and rubberbands.\n\nLowJump's 0.3425 rise and Hop's 0.1 rise are textbook matches: each starts from ground with a non-negative previous delta and ends with the feet in air, and both land inside the (0, 0.4) bound. The packet modes' 0.0625 lifts also match when the server-side move is processed as an actual position change. The 0.42 real jump escapes the deltaY < 0.4 bound by design, which is why the jump modes need NCP's jump-phase rule rather than this check. The rubberband matters beyond the violation: the S08-style teleport resets the tick sequences the packet modes rely on, breaking their per-attack state.
